prompt.adult: Psalm 22 describes those who see the speaker and ridicule Him. According to 22:7, what do they do after they shoot out the lip?
prompt.child: A psalm tells how others treated the one who was suffering. After they ridicule Him and shoot out the lip, what does 22:7 say they do?
prompt.teen: Psalm 22:7: after “they shoot out the lip,” what, “saying”?
prompt.older: According to Psalm 22:7, what do they do, after they shoot out the lip?

verses.text: All those who see Me ridicule Me; They shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying,

explanation.teen: 22:7 names ridicule, then the lip, then this action. Read the last action.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:7 also says, “All those who see Me ridicule Me.”

prompt.adult: Isaiah 53:1 asks, “Who has believed our report?” In 53:4, what does Isaiah say He has surely borne?
prompt.child: Isaiah speaks of one who suffered in the place of others. What does the verse say He has surely borne?
prompt.older: Read with 53:1, what does 53:4 say He has surely borne?

verses.text: Who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
Surely He has borne our griefs And carried our sorrows; Yet we esteemed Him stricken, Smitten by God, and afflicted.

explanation.child: Look right after “Surely He has borne” in verse 4.
explanation.teen: 53:1 is the opening question; 53:4 names what He has borne. Read that phrase.
explanation.older: It follows “Surely He has borne” in 53:4.

teaching.extended_explanation: 53:4 also says He carried our sorrows. 53:1 asks, “And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?”
teaching.takeaway: Surely He has borne our griefs.

prompt.adult: Psalm 22:11 asks that God not be far, for trouble is near. In 22:1, after “My God, My God,” what does the speaker ask?
prompt.child: The psalm opens with a cry to God, spoken twice. What does the speaker ask next?
prompt.teen: Psalm 22:1: “My God, My God, why” what?
prompt.older: Read with 22:11, what does 22:1 ask after “My God, My God, why”?

verses.text: My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me? Why are You so far from helping Me, And from the words of My groaning?
Be not far from Me, For trouble is near; For there is none to help.

explanation.child: Look right after “why” in the opening of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 22:11 asks that God not be far; 22:1 opens with a question. Read that question.
explanation.older: It follows “My God, My God, why” in 22:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:1 also asks, “Why are You so far from helping Me?” 22:11 says, “For there is none to help.”
teaching.takeaway: He asks, “why have You forsaken Me?”

prompt.adult: Isaiah 53:11 says My righteous Servant shall justify many. In 53:8, from what does Isaiah say He was cut off?
prompt.child: Isaiah says this Servant was taken from prison and from judgment. From what does the verse say He was cut off?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 53:8: “For He was cut off from” what?
prompt.older: Read with 53:11, from what does 53:8 say He was cut off?

verses.text: He was taken from prison and from judgment, And who will declare His generation? For He was cut off from the land of the living; For the transgressions of My people He was stricken.
He shall see the labor of His soul, and be satisfied. By His knowledge My righteous Servant shall justify many, For He shall bear their iniquities.

explanation.child: Look right after “cut off from” in verse 8.
explanation.teen: 53:11 speaks of justifying many; 53:8 names from what He was cut off. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 53:8 also says He was taken from prison and from judgment. 53:11 says He shall bear their iniquities.
teaching.takeaway: He was cut off from the land of the living.

prompt.adult: John 19:29 says they filled a sponge with sour wine and put it to His mouth. In 19:23, after they took His garments and made four parts, how does the verse describe the tunic?
prompt.child: The soldiers divided Jesus’ clothes at the cross. How does the verse describe His tunic?
prompt.teen: John 19:23: “Now the tunic was” what, “woven from the top in one piece”?
prompt.older: Read with 19:29, how does 19:23 say the tunic was?

verses.text: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took His garments and made four parts, to each soldier a part, and also the tunic. Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top in one piece.
Now a vessel full of sour wine was sitting there; and they filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on hyssop, and put it to His mouth.

explanation.child: Look right after “the tunic was” in verse 23.
explanation.teen: 19:29 tells of the sour wine; 19:23 describes the tunic. Read that description.

teaching.extended_explanation: 19:23 also says it was woven from the top in one piece. 19:29 says they filled a sponge with sour wine and put it to His mouth.

prompt.older: Read with John 19:37, what does Psalm 22:16 say they pierced?

My head and My bent back

verses.text: For dogs have surrounded Me; The congregation of the wicked has enclosed Me. They pierced My hands and My feet;

explanation.teen: 19:37 quotes a Scripture about piercing; 22:16 names what was pierced. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:16 also says, “For dogs have surrounded Me.” 19:37 says, “They shall look on Him whom they pierced.”
teaching.takeaway: They pierced My hands and My feet.

prompt.older: Read with Isaiah 53:6, what does John 19:33 say they did not do?

verses.text: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.

teaching.extended_explanation: 19:33 also says they saw that He was already dead. 53:6 says, “We have turned, every one, to his own way.”
teaching.takeaway: They did not break His legs.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:6 also begins, “But I am a worm, and no man.” 53:11 says He shall bear their iniquities.
